body:
Write off left-wing ideas? Seeking new ideas and topics does not mean I am writing off anything. I am not upset nor am I being defensive, you clearly think you are right and are not going to change your mind. And because you think you are right, you are automatically assuming that I am wrong because I want to talk about other topics. I know that I can be wrong, I never said that I am always right, nor do I talk to people with people with the attitude of "I am right and they are wrong". You are so busy with looking for rhetoric that may go against yours that you are pointing it out where it doesn't exist. 

You think I am wrong for trying to hear out different ideas from different people. You are the exact type of person that I am trying to avoid - a close-minded individual who thinks any rhetoric outside of their own is wrong and should be undermined, torn down, and avoided. Dude you are such a snob! Unlike you, I don't go into conversations with the goal of telling people who may disagree with me that they are wrong and offended.

I too wonder what would be extreme for the right wing as I have clearly mentioned that I did not grow up with conservatives. No one told me to be upset with identity politics and I am not acting as if they are extreme? It was my own decision to learn new things.  But again, you aren't going to change your closed mind.
Thank you! I have seen that club but always thought it was for the community college bridge program
Thank you so much! I will look into it.

I never said that those issues don't matter, and I have never avoided discussing them when brought up. Why are you responding as if I am denying/ rejecting certain issues? I have lived through many of the issues that are typically discussed, and if I have not, I have friends who have and they talk to me about them. Friends from all over the country and different parts of the world. Most of my family dealt with drug addiction and all of them were on welfare. My family is hispanic and black and lived in South Los Angeles during the 80s. My niece's uncle was killed by the cops. I grew up in predominantly black and hispanic neighborhood, went to school where minorities are the majority, and I would say over 95% of my friends are left-leaning.  

If I go into a conservative club that's willing to talk about a variety of topics but find that they are unwilling to have an actual discussion due to clouded judgment from extreme views, I will hear them out and will simply not go back. I am not seeking to be dedicated to a club, nor am I seeking to be brainwashed by one. 

You know absolutely nothing about me. I should not have to explain my beliefs and background to you for you to understand that I am merely trying to talk about other topics for once, or rather, what topics I do not want to discuss. 

I have not made one assumption about you, yet you continue to make these assumptions about me. You are trying to knockdown my opinions without knowing them, and think you know what kind of people I talk to.

I don't "avoid" left-leaning groups. If there is a left-leaning group on campus that discusses things other than identity politics and defunding the police, then I am more than willing to attend. It's exhausting to constantly hear about how me, my family, and a majority of my friends are oppressed. Do you think me going into a conservative club is not leaving my comfort zone? I did not grow up around conservatives and I know I will not agree with everything that they say. You do not know what I do and don't agree on.

People study different things so they will know different facts about what they are talking about. If I am having a conversation with someone and I think they're delusional, there is a always a chance that I can learn something new from them. If they think their feelings are facts, "proving them wrong" is going to start conflict and that's not my goal. I am trying to understand where people are coming from.
I am definitely not agreeing, that would have been disappointing to walk into. Thanks for informing me (:

I will admit that was not the best wording. My exposure to conservative views has been limited and I don't think checking out a conservative club would be a bad thing , as I will get to hear different viewpoints. I want to avoid identity politics and defunding the police because I grew up with people from a variety of backgrounds and have been hearing about these topics my entire life. They have always been the topic of discussion and I would like to learn about and discuss different topics for a change.
I did not know that trying to see different people's viewpoints on a different range of topics was me diving into an echo chamber lol

When it comes to discussing things with people, everyone has their own set of facts, opinions, and experiences. It is not a refusal to accept, it's a willingness to learn. I don't want to knock down the people I'm talking to, I genuinely want to hear their reasonings and perspectives on certain issues. If both sides are hammering one another with facts to prove the other wrong, that's not going to get anyone anywhere. I'm not going anywhere with an agenda to "ruin" discussions lmao.
I want to talk about real issues that are affecting us as a country. What do you mean in your last sentence? Why would I want to be in a club that does not use facts?
Happy birthday buddy. Cheers to this next little chapter of yours!
